title: Private Server Checkpoint Continuity
summary: R1 private current task state, bounded CAS/replay, explicit clear/prune and read-only native resume/Impact. Checkpoint text never becomes shared project authority or authenticated execution evidence.

scope.ownership: Authenticated principal plus project and slot identify private state. Project authorization is checked before stored state or source access. Administrator status does not override owner filtering. Active task/thread and source workspace/host/route/profile/selector cannot change implicitly.
scope.taskBinding: Task/thread IDs are host-declared binding guards, not independent authenticated identities. A principal may explicitly select its own exact saved binding; stronger mutually untrusted agent isolation requires distinct credentials/principals. No claim of Codex thread attestation is made.
scope.authority: The stored state is session-asserted. Canonical payload hashes detect corruption, not authentication. Currentness is assessed independently when resuming; a successful save is not durable proof that source stays current.
scope.receipts: Embedded receipts are persisted as claims only; ordinary saves reset origin. Choosing an admin producer name never grants trust. The separate opt-in receipt import in shin-authenticated-receipts-v1 confirms exact records, not names; current permission, source applicability and expiry remain mandatory.
scope.deployment: Loopback authenticated Server only, with the existing deployment identity header. No change to stable1.27.2, consumer routes, global skills, remote transport or Observer protocol.

routes.input: Optional after slot cursor and limit1..32; default16.
routes.effect: List only caller-owned metadata and server observation time; no canonical payload or implicit cleanup.
Owned metadata only; absent or other-owner slot is404/checkpoint-not-found.
Explicit native capture and private CAS save; returns metadata and replayed flag.
Read-only native resume against the saved selector's currently selected local generation.
Read-only native Impact against current selected snapshot/worktree, including untrusted saved receipts; not a complete historical diff since checkpoint.
Explicit owned CAS clear erases checkpoint payload and retains a temporary replay tombstone.
Explicitly remove only caller-owned cleared tombstones whose maximum accepted request deadline expired. Active checkpoints are never removed by this operation.

writeRequest.selector: Exact {kind: route|publication, id}; no automatic fallback or route/publication aliasing.
writeRequest.draft: Existing shin.session-draft.v1. Core creates canonical checkpoint content with its system clock. Client cannot inject a canonical checkpoint, captured_at, owner identity or trusted producer list.
writeRequest.requireCurrent: Explicit boolean. true rejects stale or incomplete source/index; false permits capture-time worktree evidence alongside a separately identified historical snapshot baseline, with no rebuild.
writeRequest.expectedRevision: Zero only for a missing slot; otherwise the exact observed global revision. An active slot cannot be rebound to another task/thread or source scope. An explicitly cleared slot may be reused with its observed tombstone revision.
writeRequest.retryIdentity: 32 lowercase hex request_id, scoped to principal/project/slot, and SHA256 of the complete canonical request. Reuse identical body on uncertain response; only the latest stored request has a replay receipt.
writeRequest.retryDeadline: Absolute Unix seconds with DB now < deadline <= now+300 and deadline above the durable retirement floor. Validate before replay and again at mutation. Expired requests are refused even if their effect previously committed; inspect metadata to resolve uncertainty. Deadline is independent of checkpoint/receipt TTL.
writeRequest.clear: The clear request uses the same task/thread/revision/request_id/deadline fields but no selector, draft or require_current. It requires no current source or live artifact.

readRequest.mismatch: Wrong task/thread is404; a different current source workspace/host/route/profile/selector is409/checkpoint-source-scope-changed. A withdrawn shared publication stays410/publication-withdrawn, never a local route fallback.
readRequest.freshness: HTTP success reports a completed assessment, not continuation approval. Inspect assessment.ok, index_current, checkpoint_age, continuation_ready, review_required and receipt trust separately. require_current=false deliberately permits drift inspection.
readRequest.projection: Server emits shin.task-resume.v1 or shin.task-impact.v1 with private checkpoint metadata, selected provenance and a transport-specific assessment schema. Host root/output coordinates and CLI next_command argv are omitted; relative verification evidence and non-executing action codes remain. It is not the full native CLI envelope.
readRequest.consistency: The private row and current publication are independently observed. An admitted read can finish after a concurrent save/clear; the response identifies its checkpoint revision and generation. There is no cross-project or source-time transaction.

storage.model: One current canonical TEXT payload per private slot, its exact SHA256 and bounded typed metadata/provenance. PostgreSQL JSONB is not used to reserialize canonical checkpoint bytes. There is no full chat or unbounded version log. Clear removes the live logical payload; it does not promise physical erasure of PostgreSQL pages, WAL or operator-owned backups.
storage.revisions: A noncycling PostgreSQL bigint sequence supplies unique increasing revisions to committed slot changes. Gaps are allowed. Ordinary callers cannot set sequence state. Deployment identity fencing remains mandatory after restore; monotonicity is not claimed across a bypassed restore or privileged database tampering.
storage.transactions: Core evaluation and filesystem access happen outside database leases. A short checkpoint-mutation advisory transaction lock serializes quota/CAS validation and writes. Recheck replay/deadline/CAS inside the write transaction before mutation; only committed records are returned. The retry deadline is an admission fence, not a hard wall-clock commit-completion or database transport deadline.
storage.integrity: Stored payload digest, envelope metadata and source binding are checked before use. Metadata readers never return canonical text or last-request hashes. Private operations keep a latest mutation receipt, not a complete general management-audit history.
storage.retention: Clear erases payload immediately. Each slot retains retry_until=max(all accepted mutation deadlines), even if a later clear has a shorter deadline. Explicit prune removes only cleared records after retry_until and atomically advances a durable global rejected-deadline floor to cover retired rows. Requests below that floor stay expired even after wall-clock rollback. No automatic TTL deletion of active task state. Recreate receives a newer global revision; stale updates cannot match a reset slot revision and still-valid older creates cannot outlive their tombstone.

hostWorkflow: Keep using the stable CLI unless the isolated Server development route is explicitly selected. Configure credentials outside projects; use existing authenticated project/route attachment and verified preparation/activation.

Build a reviewed native session draft. Choose a private slot and opaque task/thread IDs. Read current metadata to obtain the expected revision; compute a short retry deadline from current time and retain one request_id/body until the write resolves.

POST the write request. On a lost response retry the identical body within its deadline. After expiry, GET owned metadata and reconcile revision/checkpoint identity before forming a fresh request; do not regenerate a supposedly identical native checkpoint at a new clock value.

After interruption POST resume with the same task/thread and explicit currentness policy. Read relative verification paths and review drift, expiry, unresolved receipts and non-executing actions. Impact is a separate bounded source reread when needed.

Use explicit clear with the current revision when task state is no longer needed, then explicit prune after its retry deadline. Server outage does not disable existing local Core checkpoint/resume or independent Observer; this API does not silently acknowledge offline remote persistence.

sources.use: Atomic sequence allocation, permissible gaps, non-transactional sequence consumption and return only after commit. Sequence values are not a gapless event history.
Transaction advisory locks delimit short quota/CAS updates; they do not protect external source files.
